mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question: A person lifts a 10 kg box vertically upward through a height of 2 m. Another person pushes the same box horizontally across a frictionless floor for 2 m with a constant horizontal force of 10 N. Assuming g = 10 m/s², in which case is the work done greater?

options.C: Both involve the same amount of work
options.D: No work is done in either case

mcqs.explanation: Work = Force × Displacement in the direction of the force. Lifting: work = m·g·h = 10 kg × 10 m/s² × 2 m = 200 J. Pushing: work = F·d = 10 N × 2 m = 20 J. Hence the lifting case does more work.

mcqs.learning_point: Use joule as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following quantities is correctly expressed in joules (J)?
mcqs.explanation: One joule is defined as one newton‑metre (N·m). Option A matches this definition. The other options represent different physical quantities: B is a force, C is power (watt), D is speed.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines work in physics?

options.A: Work is the product of force and the displacement of the point of application of the force in the direction of the force.
options.B: Work is the energy stored in a spring when it is compressed.
options.C: Work is the rate at which energy is transferred from one system to another.
options.D: Work is the force applied irrespective of whether the object moves.

mcqs.answer: Work is the product of force and the displacement of the point of application of the force in the direction of the force.
mcqs.explanation: The definition of work requires both a force and a displacement component along the direction of that force. Options B, C, and D describe other concepts (elastic potential energy, power, and a misconception respectively).

mcqs.question: In the statement "A force of 8 N moves a crate 4 m to the right", which quantity represents the displacement?
mcqs.explanation: Displacement is the distance moved in a specified direction; here it is 4 m. The 8 N is the magnitude of the force, while the direction is part of the displacement vector but not the scalar distance itself.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand conditions for work to be done
mcqs.question: Work is done on an object only when:

options.A: A force acts on the object
options.C: The force has a component along the direction of displacement

mcqs.answer: The force has a component along the direction of displacement
mcqs.explanation: For work to be done, there must be a component of the applied force in the direction of the object's displacement. Merely having a force (A) or motion (B) is insufficient if the force is perpendicular to the motion. Option D is opposite to the requirement.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate work using W = Fs for simple cases
mcqs.question: A constant force of 15 N pushes a crate along a straight line for 3 m in the direction of the force. What is the work done on the crate?
mcqs.explanation: Work = Force × Displacement = 15 N × 3 m = 45 J. The force and displacement are collinear, so the full product contributes to work. Options B, C, and D are incorrect calculations.

mcqs.learning_point: Use joule as the SI unit
mcqs.question: A constant force of 4 N pushes a block through a distance of 5 m. What is the work done on the block?
mcqs.explanation: Work = Force × Displacement = 4 N × 5 m = 20 J. The joule (J) is the SI unit for work. The other options result from incorrect multiplication or neglecting the definition.

mcqs.question: A person pushes a stationary wall with a force of 30 N, but the wall does not move. According to the definition of work, how much work is done by the person on the wall?
mcqs.explanation: Work requires displacement. Since the wall does not move, displacement is zero, so work = Force × 0 = 0 J, regardless of the magnitude of the applied force. Options B and C incorrectly assume work without displacement, and D is unnecessary.
